text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA
- Banca Transilvania is to apply to be listed on the Bucharest stock exchange.
ECONOMISTUL
- The newspaper publishes a two-page report on energy consumption in rural areas.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Striking coalminers and government representatives concluded a draft protocol which is to be accepted by the protesters in the western Jiu Valley coalfield.
- The state will take over 15 percent of the energy costs of profitable companies, said Reform Minister Ulm Spineanu.
ADEVARUL
- As many as 30 investors want to buy shares of the Petromidia oil refinery, says the newspaper in a report on the company.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The newspaper publishes the draft of a law under which private farmers would be compensated for farm equipment confiscated by the communists.
- The newspaper publishes the bill under which farm land would be distributed to young families to attract them to rural areas from towns where they often are jobless.
- Under a new taxation bill, the profit tax for Romanian investors would be around 15 to 25 percent, Spineanu said.
General:
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The Romanian Orthodox church protests against a Senate decision under which several former Greek Catholic churches, confiscated by the communists in 1947, would be returned to Greek Catholics.
- Workers at Roman SA truck maker protest against the restructuring programme.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Coalminers blocked highways to demand pay rises and protest against the government's pledges to restructure their loss-making mining sector.
- The government asked parliament to annul 517 laws dating from the former communist era.
- The newspaper publishes a full-page report on drug smuggling and consumption in Romania.
ADEVARUL
- The upper house, the Senate, adopted a bill to return to the Jewish community some of the properties confiscated by the former communists.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- As many as 125 radio stations, 55 television stations and 938 cable television companies function in Romania, said a report from the National Broadcasters Council.
-- Bucharest Newsroom, 40-1 3120264
